question.problem: Determine the points where the ellipse ${x}^{2}+3{y}^{2}-6x+12y=7$ intercepts the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
To calculate the $x$-intercepts, we need to substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the ellipse and solve the resulting equation for $x.$ We do this and solve the resulting equation by completing the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+3{y}^{2}-6x+12y & =7 \\ {x}^{2}+3(0)^{2}-6x+12(0) & =7 \\ {x}^{2}-6x & =7 \\ ({x}^{2}-6x+9)-9 & =7 \\ (x-3)^{2} & =16 \\ x-3 & =\pm \sqrt{16} \\ x & =3\pm 4 \\ x & =-1,7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the ellipse intercepts the $x$-axis at $(-1,0)$ and $(7,0).$
